lyrics:
[Intro: scratchy four-chord guitar riff alone, then drums crash in]

[Verse 1: quiet, mumbled, two-note guitar, bass and drums]
Bring the snacks and bring the blame
Everybody's got the same new name
I was cool for half a week
Now I'm famous in my sleep

[Pre-Chorus: building, one word over and over]
Whatever, whatever, whatever, wait
Whatever, whatever, is it too late?

[Chorus: loud, screamed, wall of distorted guitar]
Turn the lights down, we're on fire
Read the room, the room's a liar
I feel stupid, I feel fine
Stand in line for a lukewarm riot
A little bored, a little wired
Oh well, as you were

[Verse 2: quiet, mumbled, two-note guitar]
I'm the best at being worst
Raised my hand and still got cursed
All my heroes sell me shoes
I forget which side I choose

[Pre-Chorus: building, one word over and over]
Whatever, whatever, whatever, wait
Whatever, whatever, is it too late?

[Chorus: loud, screamed, wall of distorted guitar]
Turn the lights down, we're on fire
Read the room, the room's a liar
I feel stupid, I feel fine
Stand in line for a lukewarm riot
A little bored, a little wired
Oh well, as you were

[Guitar Solo: plays the verse melody, simple, watery chorus effect]

[Verse 3: quiet, mumbled, voice cracking]
Found a cause and lost the thread
Signed a wall that someone read
It's a joke until it's not
Tell my mother what I bought

[Pre-Chorus: building, one word over and over]
Whatever, whatever, whatever, wait
Whatever, whatever, is it too late?

[Final Chorus: loudest, voice shredding]
Turn the lights down, we're on fire
Read the room, the room's a liar
I feel stupid, I feel fine
Stand in line for a lukewarm riot
A little bored, a little wired
Oh well, as you were

[Outro: screamed over the riff, feedback, sudden stop]
As you were
As you were
As you were
As you were
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 117 BPM, 4/4, F minor. Four power chords the whole way through. Sullen verses, explosive choruses.

VOICE: Male, hoarse and sandpapery. Verses mumbled and slurred on purpose, low in the mix. Choruses screamed at the top of the range until the voice breaks. Doubled in the chorus only.

INSTRUMENTS: One electric guitar: a scratchy, percussive strum of muted strings between chords in the intro, a clean two-note figure through a watery chorus pedal in the verses, then full fuzz distortion. Driving, melodic bass that carries the verses. Hard-hit live drums with a flam on the snare and wide open hi-hats in the chorus. Nothing else.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, riff alone for 4 bars, then a drum fill and the full band. 0:25 Verse 1, drops to bass, drums and the two-note guitar. 0:50 Pre-chorus, building. 1:06 Chorus 1, everything loud. 1:31 Verse 2. 1:56 Pre-chorus. 2:12 Chorus 2. 2:37 Guitar solo that simply plays the verse tune. 2:53 Verse 3. 3:10 Pre-chorus. 3:26 Final chorus. 3:51 Outro, the last line screamed four times, feedback, hard stop at 4:05.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Punchy early-90s rock production: dry, loud, drums huge and natural, guitars doubled left and right, almost no reverb.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The drum fill at 0:08 that throws the whole band onto the riff.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The targets are current (attention, outrage, heroes who sell things) and the last verse lets a parent in. The joke is that the anger is real and the riot is only room temperature.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Boredom, contempt, release, and a shrug.

WHAT IT IS ABOUT

A crowd that is angry and bored in equal measure queues up for a protest that is only mildly warm. Nobody is sure what it is about, including the singer.

THE OTHER WAYS TO HEAR IT

Hear it as: teenagers today, outraged and scrolling; their parents, who were the originals and now have mortgages; a satire of online fury; or a sincere anthem. It supports all four.

ENGINEERED HOOKS AND THE DESIGNED MISHEARING

Borrowed mechanics: quiet-loud-quiet, four heavy chords, self-cancelling couplets, a one-word pre-chorus and a title that is a joke. Designed mishearing: the verses are meant to be slurred, and 'a lukewarm riot' comes out as 'a new one, right?', which is exactly what each generation says about its anger.
